mainTopic: When a בית דין is liable for a mistaken ruling: not for uprooting a whole מצוה, and not for something the צדוקים agree with; also סומכוס's משל and בן עזאי's question.
overview: The גמרא first explains why a person who relied on the בית דין after it took back its ruling must bring an אשם תלוי: he could have asked and found out. Then רבי יוסי בר אבין compares סומכוס's view to an offering brought at בין השמשות, a doubt nobody can answer, so no אשם תלוי is brought. Next the גמרא asks why בן עזאי needed to ask רבי עקיבא his question, and רבא answers that they argue about a traveler who set out but is still in town. A ברייתא then learns from "וְנֶעֱלַם דָּבָר" that a ruling uprooting a whole מצוה brings no קרבן, while permitting one detail does. עולא, חזקיה and רב אשי each give a source for this. Finally רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules that the בית דין is not liable for a matter the צדוקים agree with, since even schoolchildren know it. The גמרא defends this rule against the משנה's cases of נדה, שבת and עבודה זרה by showing that each mistaken ruling permitted a detail the פסוק does not openly state.

steps.title: Even if the court brings the offering, he could have asked
steps.stepSummary: The view that the person must bring an אשם תלוי holds even according to the opinion that the בית דין, and not the ציבור, brings the offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no need to say this according to the view that the ציבור brings the offering, because then the court's change of ruling becomes public. It is true even according to the view that the בית דין brings the offering, where the change does not become public. Still, if he had asked, people would have told him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the approach just stated, that he connects his act to himself and must bring an אשם תלוי, fits both opinions about who brings the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ציבור brings the offering, everyone knows the court changed its ruling, so the person is clearly at fault. Even if only the בית דין brings it and the change is not public, he still could have asked and found out. So his mistake counts as his own, not the court's.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not necessary to say. The easy case is mentioned first, then the harder case.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the next step. Here the 'not necessary' case is the ציבור view. In step 3 the order is flipped and the 'not necessary' case is the בית דין view.

phrases.english: And it is not necessary to say this according to the one who said
the congregation brings the offering, since then the matter is publicized.
phrases.notes: The 'matter' is that the court took back its ruling.

phrases.english: But even according to the one who said

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית דִּין מְבִיאִין, דְּלָא מְפַרְסְמָא מִלְּתָא –
phrases.english: the court brings the offering, where the matter is not publicized

phrases.aramaic: אִי הֲוָה שָׁאֵיל, הֲווֹ אָמְרִין לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: if he had asked, they would have told him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא מִבַּעְיָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר צִבּוּר מַיְיתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier explanation that the person ties his act to himself and is liable for an אשם תלוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under both opinions about who brings the offering, he could have asked and found out, so he is liable for an אשם תלוי.

steps.title: The analogy of the offering brought at twilight
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין compares סומכוס's case to someone who brought his atonement offering at בין השמשות. That person does not bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר אבין, and some say רבי יוסי בר זבידא, said: Here is a משל for סומכוס's view. A person brought his atonement offering at twilight. Maybe it was still day and the offering worked, and maybe it was already night and it did not. Still, he does not bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives a comparison that explains סומכוס's view: in this kind of doubt there is no אשם תלוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a doubt about a sin that would need a חטאת brings an אשם תלוי. But a doubt about בין השמשות can never be cleared up, so it is not a normal doubt and no אשם תלוי is brought. The person who relied on the court is compared to this case, so he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Twilight, when it is unclear whether it is day or night.
A guilt offering brought when it is unsure whether one sinned.

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the other side: according to סומכוס, the person who relied on the court is not liable for an אשם תלוי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin said,
and some say it was Rabbi Yosei bar Zevida:
An analogy for Sumakhos: to what is this matter comparable?
To a person who brought his atonement offering at twilight,
it is uncertain whether he was atoned for while it was still day,
or uncertain whether he was atoned for after it became dark,
where he does not bring a provisional guilt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the approach that makes him liable, this gives an analogy that explains סומכוס as exempting him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Twilight is a doubt that can never be cleared up and brings no אשם תלוי. סומכוס's case is like it.

steps.title: The analogy works even if the change was public
steps.stepSummary: The משל fits even the view that the ציבור brings the offering, because in the twilight case nobody could ever answer his question.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no need to say this according to the view that the בית דין brings the offering, where the change is not public. It is true even according to the view that the ציבור brings it, where the change is public and we would have told him. The reason is that at twilight, whether it was day or night, even if he asked he would find nobody who could answer him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the twilight משל holds under both opinions, the mirror image of step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the משל fails under the ציבור view, since there he could have asked and found out. The גמרא answers that the twilight case is a doubt with no one to ask, and that kind of doubt does not bring an אשם תלוי. So the comparison stands under both opinions.
steps.whatToRemember: Step 1: he is liable because he could have asked. Step 3: the twilight משל means no אשם תלוי, because nobody can answer that question.

phrases.english: And it is not necessary to say this according to the one who said

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית דִּין מְבִיאִין דְּלָא אִפַּרְסְמָא מִלְּתָא,
phrases.english: the court brings the offering, where the matter was not publicized,
but even according to the one who said
the congregation brings the offering, where the matter is publicized,
and we would have told him,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָכָא בְּסָפֵק מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם סָפֵק מִשֶּׁחָשֵׁכָה,
phrases.english: because here, in a doubt whether it was still day or after dark,

phrases.aramaic: אִי שָׁאֵיל לָא אַשְׁכַּח אִינָשׁ דִּמְשַׁיֵּילֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: if he asks, he would not find a person he could ask.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא מִבַּעְיָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בֵּית דִּין מְבִיאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the twilight analogy of step 2 to cover both opinions about who brings the offering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The twilight analogy holds even under the ציבור view, because a doubt that nobody can answer brings no אשם תלוי.

steps.title: Quoting בן עזאי's question from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה where בן עזאי asks רבי עקיבא how the traveler is different from someone who stayed home.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי said to him: How is this case different from the one who sits at home, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. The question about it comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, someone who went overseas is exempt and someone who stayed home is liable. בן עזאי asks what the difference is. רבי עקיבא answers that the one at home could have heard about the court's change, but the traveler could not.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who sits, meaning who stays at home.

phrases.english: Ben Azzai said to him:
What is the difference from one who sits at home, etc.
phrases.notes: כו׳ means 'and so on'. The rest of the line, with רבי עקיבא's answer, is in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ בֶּן עַזַּאי מַאי שְׁנָא מִן הַיּוֹשֵׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes בן עזאי's question about the traveler compared with the one who stayed home.

steps.title: Why did בן עזאי need to ask?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: רבי עקיבא's answer is so clearly correct, so how could בן עזאי not have seen it himself?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא answered בן עזאי well, didn't he? Then what was בן עזאי's question?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's exchange. If the answer is so obvious, why would a great scholar like בן עזאי ask the question?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is not that רבי עקיבא was wrong. Because his answer seems so simple, בן עזאי's question must have meant something deeper. The גמרא now has to explain what he was really asking.
steps.confusionAlert: This looks like praise for רבי עקיבא, but it works as a challenge. If the answer is that good, why did בן עזאי ask?

phrases.aramaic: שַׁפִּיר קָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְבֶן עַזַּאי?
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva answered ben Azzai well, did he not?

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁפִּיר קָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְבֶן עַזַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the exchange quoted in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: בן עזאי's question in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא's answer, that the one at home could have heard and the traveler could not, is so obvious that בן עזאי should not have needed to ask.

steps.title: רבא: they argue about someone who set out but is still in town
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the argument is about a person who has started his trip but has not yet left his city. בן עזאי says he is liable and רבי עקיבא says he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There is a difference between them when the person has set out on the road. According to בן עזאי he is liable, since he is still at home. According to רבי עקיבא he is exempt, since he has already set out on his way.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from step 5. בן עזאי was not missing something obvious, because the case is a man who has started his trip but is still in his own town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the man were already overseas, everyone would agree he could not hear that the בית דין took back its ruling. Here he is still in town, so בן עזאי says he is like someone sitting at home. רבי עקיבא says his busy travel plans already count as being away.

keyTerms.meaning: Set out on the road: started his journey
There is a difference between them
He is still at his home

steps.whatToRemember: בן עזאי and רבי עקיבא only argue about a traveler who is still in his own town. Once he is truly far away, the difference is obvious.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Someone who set out on the road: there is a difference between them.
phrases.notes: He has started his trip but hasn't left his town yet.

phrases.english: According to בן עזאי, he is liable,
since he is still at his home.
According to רבי עקיבא, he is exempt,
since he has already set out on the road.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הֶחְזִיק בַּדֶּרֶךְ אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the traveler is still in his own city.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case is a man already overseas, so רבי עקיבא's answer seems too obvious to argue with.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is a man who set out but is still in town, and that is a real point of argument.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the court ruled to uproot the whole מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה: the בית דין ruled to uproot an entire מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The בית דין ruled for him to uproot the entire body of the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the next words of the משנה. This sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that if the בית דין rules that a whole מצוה does not apply, the judges do not bring the special קרבן for a mistaken ruling. The next step brings the source for this.

keyTerms.meaning: The entire body, meaning the whole מצוה

phrases.english: The court ruled for him
to uproot the entire body of the מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹרוּ לוֹ בֵּית דִּין לַעֲקוֹר אֶת כָּל הַגּוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ruling that uproots an entire מצוה does not obligate the בית דין to bring a קרבן.

steps.title: ברייתא: no קרבן when they deny a whole מצוה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from "וְנֶעֱלַם דָּבָר" that if the בית דין says a whole מצוה like נדה, שבת or עבודה זרה is not in the Torah, they are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: "And a matter is hidden" means only part of a מצוה, not that the whole מצוה is uprooted. How so? If they said there is no נדה in the Torah, no שבת in the Torah, or no עבודה זרה in the Torah, you might think they are liable. So the verse says "And a matter is hidden", and not that the whole מצוה is hidden. These judges are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the Torah source for the משנה's rule. A ruling that wipes out a whole מצוה does not bring a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word דָּבָר, "a matter", points to one piece of a מצוה being hidden from the judges. Saying that שבת does not exist at all is not a hidden detail. Everyone knows שבת is in the Torah, so this is not the kind of mistake the קרבן covers.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"And a matter is hidden"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:13

phrases.english: but not that the entire מצוה is uprooted.
How so?
If they said: There is no נדה in the Torah,
there is no Shabbat in the Torah,
there is no idol worship in the Torah,
one might think they would be liable.
So the verse says: "And a matter is hidden",
and not that an entire מצוה is hidden.
So these judges are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וְנֶעֱלַם דָּבָר וְלֹא שֶׁיֵּעָקֵר הַמִּצְוָה כּוּלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the verse that is the source for the משנה quoted in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's rule that uprooting a whole מצוה brings no קרבן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 4:13, "וְנֶעֱלַם דָּבָר", read as one hidden detail rather than a whole מצוה.

steps.title: ברייתא: canceling only one detail does bring a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: If the בית דין agrees that the מצוה exists but permits one part of it, the judges are liable, also learned from "וְנֶעֱלַם דָּבָר".
steps.simpleTranslation: But if they said: There is נדה in the Torah, but someone with a שומרת יום כנגד יום is exempt. There is שבת in the Torah, but carrying from a private area to a public area is exempt. There is עבודה זרה in the Torah, but bowing is exempt. You might think they are exempt. So the verse says "And a matter is hidden", and not the whole body.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the opposite case. When the judges keep the מצוה but cancel one piece of it, they are liable to bring the קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the real "hidden matter": one detail of the law was hidden from the judges while they still kept the rest of the מצוה. The examples are one detail each from נדה, שבת and עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who must watch one clean day for a day she saw blood
One who carries from a private area to a public area
One who bows down to an idol

steps.whatToRemember: Denying a whole מצוה brings no קרבן. Permitting one detail while keeping the מצוה does bring a קרבן.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two "exempts". In these examples "exempt" is what the judges wrongly ruled about the sinner. The judges themselves are liable for that ruling.

phrases.english: But if they said: There is נדה in the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַבָּא עַל שׁוֹמֶרֶת יוֹם כְּנֶגֶד יוֹם פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: but one who has relations with a woman who watches a day for a day is exempt;
there is Shabbat in the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַמּוֹצִיא מֵרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: but one who carries out from a private domain to a public domain is exempt;
there is idol worship in the Torah,
but one who bows down is exempt.
One might think the judges would be exempt.
So the verse says: "And a matter is hidden",
and not the entire body.
phrases.notes: So a ruling about one detail is exactly the case where the judges bring a קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the same ברייתא, giving the opposite case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Permitting one detail of a מצוה while keeping the rest makes the בית דין liable for a קרבן.

steps.title: How could anyone think the judges would be exempt here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if they were exempt for a partial ruling too, there would be no case at all where they are liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: "One might think they would be exempt." But if they are exempt when they keep part and cancel part, and also exempt when they uproot the whole body, in what case would they ever be liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording "you might think they are exempt" in the second half of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half already said that uprooting a whole מצוה is exempt. If a partial ruling were exempt too, no ruling would ever bring the קרבן. That makes the Torah's קרבן pointless, so how could the ברייתא even suggest it?

keyTerms.meaning: Keeping part of the מצוה and canceling part
In what case would they be liable?

phrases.english: The Master said: "One might think they would be exempt."

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי בְּקִיּוּם מִקְצָת וּבִיטּוּל מִקְצָת פְּטוּרִין,
phrases.english: But if when keeping part and canceling part they are exempt,
and when uprooting the entire body they are exempt,
in what case are they liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase "יָכוֹל יְהוּ פְּטוּרִין" in the second half of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both a whole ruling and a partial ruling were exempt, there would be no case left for the קרבן, so the suggestion makes no sense.

steps.title: The real question: maybe "דבר" means the whole thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the תנא really meant to ask whether "דבר" includes a whole מצוה, so that even uprooting it would make the judges liable. The verse teaches otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what was bothering the תנא: You might say that "דבר" means an entire matter. So the verse says: "And a matter is hidden."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's "you might think" was really a different question. Perhaps the word דָּבָר covers an entire מצוה, which would make the judges liable even for uprooting it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא never truly considered making the partial case exempt. Its doubt was whether "דבר" could mean a whole topic. The verse's wording shows it means only a part, so liability is limited to partial rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what was bothering the תנא

steps.whatToRemember: The word דָּבָר limits the קרבן to a ruling that cancels part of a מצוה, never a ruling that uproots all of it.

phrases.english: This is what was difficult for the תנא:
Say that "a matter" means the entire matter!
So the verse says: "And a matter is hidden."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 by explaining what the ברייתא really meant.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seriously suggested that a partial ruling is exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא was really asking whether דָּבָר includes a whole מצוה. The verse shows it means only part of one.

steps.title: How does the verse show this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how "וְנֶעֱלַם דָּבָר" teaches that only a partial ruling makes the judges liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where is this understood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the words of the פסוק actually show the rule from Step 11. This question sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said the verse limits liability to a partial ruling, but the plain word "דָּבָר" does not obviously mean "part of a matter." The גמרא wants to know which detail in the verse teaches that limit.

keyTerms.meaning: From where is it understood? (a request for how a verse teaches something)

phrases.english: From where is it inferred?
phrases.notes: He means: how do the words "וְנֶעֱלַם דָּבָר" show that it is only part of a מצוה, not the whole thing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the textual basis of the conclusion reached in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which detail in "וְנֶעֱלַם דָּבָר" limits liability to a partial ruling.

steps.title: עולא reads the verse as part of a matter
steps.stepSummary: עולא reads the verse as "וְנֶעֱלַם מִדָּבָר", meaning that only part of the matter was hidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Read it as "וְנֶעֱלַם מִדָּבָר", meaning part of a matter was hidden from them.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers by reading the letter מ at the end of "וְנֶעֱלַם" a second time, at the start of "דָּבָר". The phrase then means "part of a matter was hidden."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letter מ in front of a word can mean "from" or "part of." So "מִדָּבָר" tells us the judges missed only part of the מצוה. If they erased the whole מצוה, it is not this case.

keyTerms.meaning: Read it as (reading extra meaning into the verse's letters)
From a matter, meaning part of a matter

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Read into it: "And part of a matter was hidden."
phrases.notes: The מ that ends "וְנֶעֱלַם" is read a second time, as if it also starts the next word.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Reading the verse as "מִדָּבָר" shows it is talking about part of a matter.

steps.title: חזקיה learns it from 'of all the מצוות'
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה gives another source: "מִכׇּל מִצְוֹת" means some of the מצוות, not all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: The verse says "and they did one of all the מצוות". "Of all the מצוות" means part, not all of the מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה offers a different source from another part of the same פסוק. The word "of" (מִן) in "מִכׇּל" shows the error covers only part of the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like עולא, חזקיה builds on the letter מ meaning "part of." He finds it in a word that is clearly written, "מִכׇּל", so he does not need to read a letter twice.

keyTerms.meaning: Of all the מצוות, meaning some of them

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya said: The verse states:
"And they did one of all the מצוות"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:13

phrases.english: "Of all the מצוות", and not all the מצוות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to Step 12, using a different word in the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "מִכׇּל מִצְוֹת" limits liability to part of the law.

steps.title: But 'מצוות' means at least two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that "מִצְוֹת" is plural, so uprooting one whole מצוה would still be only part of two.
steps.simpleTranslation: But "מצוות" means at least two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges חזקיה's source. Because "מִצְוֹת" is plural, the verse could include uprooting one whole מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "part of the מצוות" means part of two or more מצוות, then one entire מצוה counts as "part." That would make the judges liable even for uprooting a whole מצוה, which is the opposite of what חזקיה wanted to prove.

phrases.english: "מצוות" indicates two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks חזקיה's source from Step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A plural word means one whole מצוה could be "part of" the מצוות, so the verse would not exclude uprooting a whole מצוה.

steps.title: The word is written as singular
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the word is spelled "מִצְוַת", like a singular.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The word is written "מצות" without the second ו, as if it were singular.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק defends חזקיה. The word is read as plural, but its spelling looks singular.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of the spelling, the verse means "part of a single מצוה." So uprooting the whole מצוה is still excluded, and חזקיה's source stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written (how the word is spelled in the Torah)

steps.confusionAlert: How a word is read aloud and how it is spelled can differ. Here the spelling (singular) teaches the law, even though it is read as plural.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
"Mitzvat" is written.
phrases.notes: In the Torah scroll the word is spelled without the second ו, so it looks like one מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: ״מִצְוַת״ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Spelling-based reading (written form versus read form).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural "מִצְוֹת" would include uprooting one whole מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The singular spelling means part of one מצוה, so a whole מצוה is excluded.

steps.title: רב אשי learns it from the rebellious elder
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי learns it through a גזירה שוה on the word "דָּבָר" from זקן ממרא, who is liable only for part of a matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We learn "דבר" here from "דבר" by זקן ממרא. There it says "If a matter is too hard for you... do not turn from the matter they tell you, right or left." Just as זקן ממרא is about part of a matter and not a whole matter, so too a ruling of בית דין must be about part of a matter and not the whole thing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third source. He compares the word "דָּבָר" here to the same word in the section about זקן ממרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זקן ממרא is only guilty when he argues over part of a law, not over a whole law. Through a גזירה שוה, the same limit carries over to the ruling of the בית דין. They are liable only when the error was about part of a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: A rebellious elder, a sage who rules against the High Court
Learning one law from another through a shared word
The whole body of the מצוה, its entire essence

steps.whatToRemember: Three sources teach that the בית דין is liable only for permitting part of a מצוה: עולא reads "מִדָּבָר", חזקיה reads "מִכׇּל מִצְוַת", and רב אשי uses a גזירה שוה from זקן ממרא.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
He derives "matter" "matter" from the rebellious elder,
as it is written about the rebellious elder:
"If a matter is too hard for you...
phrases.notes: דברים 17:8–11

phrases.aramaic: לֹא תָסוּר מִן הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר יַגִּידוּ לְךָ
phrases.english: You shall not turn aside from the matter that they tell you,
right or left."

phrases.aramaic: מָה מַמְרֵא – ״מִן הַדָּבָר״ וְלֹא כׇּל דָּבָר,
phrases.english: Just as the rebellious elder is about "from the matter" and not a whole matter,
so too with a ruling: "a matter" and not the entire essence.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: יָלֵיף ״דָּבָר״ ״דָּבָר״ מִזָּקֵן מַמְרֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third, independent answer to Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from זקן ממרא, who is guilty only for part of a matter.

steps.title: No liability for something the Sadducees agree to
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the בית דין is liable only for a mistaken ruling the צדוקים would not agree with.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The בית דין is not liable unless they rule on something the צדוקים do not agree with. If they rule on something the צדוקים agree with, they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from שמואל that further limits when the בית דין is liable. It only applies to mistakes in laws that are not plainly written in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צדוקים accepted only the plain words of the Written Torah. If a law is so clear that even they accept it, a court that permits it has not made a real ruling. Liability applies only to a mistake in a law that depends on the Oral Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: A sect that accepted only the plain Written Torah and rejected the Oral Torah

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a second boundary for בית דין liability. Besides not uprooting a whole מצוה, the error must be in something that is not obvious from the plain verse.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says that Shmuel says:
A court is not liable
unless they rule on a matter
that the Sadducees do not agree with.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּדָבָר שֶׁהַצַּדּוּקִין מוֹדִין בּוֹ – פְּטוּרִין.
phrases.english: But for a matter that the Sadducees agree with, they are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֵין בֵּית דִּין חַיָּיבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: another limit on when the בית דין is liable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בית דין is liable only for a mistaken ruling the צדוקים would reject. For a matter the צדוקים accept, the judges are exempt.

steps.title: What is the reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a ruling on something the צדוקים agree to is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind שמואל's rule. This sets up the short answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not obvious why a plainly written law should bring exemption rather than liability. The גמרא wants the logic behind it.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why judges are exempt for a mistake in a law that the צדוקים also accept.

steps.title: Even schoolchildren know it
steps.stepSummary: The answer: something even children learn in school is not a real ruling, so the judges are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Go read it in a children's school; it is something everyone knows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that such a law is so basic that a child in school knows it. A mistake about it is plain ignorance, not a ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The special קרבן of the בית דין is brought for a real legal ruling that went wrong. Permitting something obviously written in the Torah does not count as a ruling at all, so the judges are exempt.
steps.whatToRemember: For the בית דין to be liable, the mistaken ruling must be about part of a מצוה, and it must be something not obvious from the plain verse. Something every schoolchild knows is not a real ruling.

phrases.english: It is "go read it in the schoolhouse."
phrases.notes: It's so basic that children learning חומש in school already know it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A law even schoolchildren know is not counted as a ruling; a mistake about it is just ignorance.

steps.title: The משנה's case of שומרת יום כנגד יום seems to contradict שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says judges are liable for permitting a שומרת יום כנגד יום. But that law is written in the Torah, so even the צדוקים agree with it. According to שמואל, the judges should be exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: if the judges ruled that the Torah forbids a נדה, but someone who has relations with a שומרת יום כנגד יום is exempt, they are liable. But why are they liable? The law of a שומרת יום כנגד יום is written in the Torah: 'And she shall count for herself.' This teaches that she counts one clean day for one day of bleeding. So even the צדוקים would agree with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a case from our משנה to attack שמואל's rule from the last steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said the judges are liable only for a mistake about something the צדוקים would not agree with. The law of a שומרת יום כנגד יום comes straight from a פסוק, so even the צדוקים accept it. Yet the משנה makes the judges liable for permitting her, which seems to contradict שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who saw blood outside her regular period and must wait one clean day for each day she saw
A woman who is impure because of her monthly period
'And she shall count for herself', the פסוק about counting clean days

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'פטור' here is part of the judges' mistaken ruling. They said such a person is exempt. The משנה itself says the judges are liable for ruling that way.

phrases.english: We learned in the משנה:
There is a prohibition of a menstruating woman in the Torah,
phrases.notes: This is the start of what the judges ruled. The משנה says they are liable for this ruling.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַבָּא עַל שׁוֹמֶרֶת יוֹם כְּנֶגֶד יוֹם פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: but one who has relations with a woman who watches a day for a day is exempt.
And why should the judges be liable?

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹמֶרֶת יוֹם כְּנֶגֶד יוֹם, הָא כְּתִיב
phrases.english: A woman who watches a day for a day: it is written,
"And she shall count for herself,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:28

phrases.english: which teaches that she counts one clean day for one day!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: יֵשׁ נִדָּה בַּתּוֹרָה, אֲבָל הַבָּא עַל שׁוֹמֶרֶת יוֹם כְּנֶגֶד יוֹם פָּטוּר. וְאַמַּאי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's rule, which was just explained in step 20, using a case from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that judges are exempt when they rule on something the צדוקים agree with.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The law of a שומרת יום כנגד יום is written in a פסוק, so the צדוקים agree with it. Yet the משנה makes the judges liable for permitting her.

steps.title: The judges only permitted the initial stage of relations
steps.stepSummary: The judges did not deny the whole law. They ruled that only completed relations are forbidden and that the initial stage (העראה) is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה means a case where the judges said: the initial stage is permitted; only completed relations are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל. It says the judges' mistake was smaller than it first looked: they permitted only העראה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the judges had denied the whole law of a שומרת יום כנגד יום, they would be exempt under שמואל. So the גמרא says they permitted only the partial act. That detail might not be obvious to the צדוקים.

phrases.english: It is a case where they said: the initial stage of relations is permitted;
it is only completed relations that is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 21 by narrowing what the judges ruled.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case in the משנה (אוקימתא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The judges denied the whole law of a שומרת יום כנגד יום, which is written in the Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: The judges permitted only העראה. That is not openly stated, so they are liable.

steps.title: העראה is also written in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that answer, because a פסוק explicitly forbids even העראה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is also written in the Torah: 'He has uncovered her source'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer in step 22. The ban on העראה is also in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הֶעֱרָה in the פסוק points to the initial stage of relations. So that law is written openly too, and the צדוקים would agree with it. The judges should still be exempt under שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He has uncovered her source', the פסוק showing that even the initial stage is forbidden

phrases.english: This too is written:
"He has uncovered her source"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:18. The word הֶעֱרָה sounds like הַעֲרָאָה, the initial stage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the judges permitted העראה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק openly forbids העראה, so the צדוקים would agree, and the judges should be exempt.

steps.title: The judges permitted relations in an atypical manner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a new case. The judges forbade only normal relations and permitted relations שלא כדרכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where they said: relations in the normal way are forbidden, but relations not in the normal way are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second try at explaining the judges' mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the mistake is about the manner of relations, not the stage. The idea is that permitting relations שלא כדרכה is not written openly in the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in the normal way (anal relations)

phrases.english: It is a case where they said: in the normal way, it is forbidden;
not in the normal way, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that step 23 rejected with a new version of the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The judges permitted העראה, but that is written openly.
steps.terutzMaskana: The judges permitted relations שלא כדרכה.

steps.title: Atypical relations are also written in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this answer too. The plural 'ways of lying with a woman' includes both kinds of relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'the ways of lying with a woman'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second answer with another פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural word מִשְׁכְּבֵי ('ways of lying') shows that the Torah counts both normal and atypical relations. So this law is written openly too, and the problem from step 21 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The ways of lying with a woman', in the plural, covering both kinds of relations

phrases.english: But it is written: "the ways of lying with a woman"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:22. Notice the plural, "ways": more than one kind of relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the judges permitted relations שלא כדרכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural in the פסוק shows atypical relations are included in the ban. So it is written openly, and the judges should be exempt.

steps.title: The judges permitted only the initial stage of atypical relations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא combines the two ideas. The judges permitted only העראה, and only שלא כדרכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where they said: in the normal way, even the initial stage is forbidden. Not in the normal way, only completed relations are forbidden, but the initial stage is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer. It joins the two rejected ideas into one narrow mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק on its own covers one point: העראה is forbidden, and atypical relations are forbidden. Neither פסוק openly says that העראה in an atypical manner is forbidden. So a ruling permitting exactly that is not plainly written, and the judges can be liable.
steps.whatToRemember: This combined case (העראה שלא כדרכה) avoids the two פסוקים, but it does not last. Step 27 challenges it, and step 28 replaces it with a different case.

phrases.english: It is a case where they said: in the normal way, even the initial stage is forbidden;

phrases.aramaic: בְּשֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ – גְּמַר בִּיאָה הוּא דְּאָסוּר,
phrases.english: not in the normal way, it is only completed relations that is forbidden,
but the initial stage is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25 by joining the ideas from steps 22 and 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The judges permitted העראה, or atypical relations, and each of those is written openly.
steps.terutzMaskana: The judges permitted only העראה in an atypical manner. That is not openly written, so they are liable.

steps.title: Then the משנה could have used a plain נדה
steps.stepSummary: If the mistake is about העראה שלא כדרכה, it would apply to a נדה too. So why does the משנה speak about a שומרת יום כנגד יום?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even with a נדה the judges would be liable too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the new case for now. But it asks why the משנה chose a שומרת יום כנגד יום as its example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה contrasts a נדה (forbidden) with a שומרת יום כנגד יום (wrongly permitted). But if the mistake is only about העראה שלא כדרכה, it fits a נדה just as well. So the specific choice of a שומרת יום כנגד יום no longer makes sense.

phrases.english: If so, then even with a menstruating woman as well!
phrases.notes: He means: a ruling permitting this act with a regular נדה should also make the judges liable. So why did the משנה pick a שומרת יום כנגד יום?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 26 based on the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case given in step 26 as the explanation of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The mistake described in step 26 applies equally to a נדה, so the משנה's choice of a שומרת יום כנגד יום has no reason.

steps.title: The judges said the העראה prohibition applies only to a נדה
steps.stepSummary: The case is normal relations. The judges ruled that the ban on העראה is written only about a נדה (אשה דוה), so a שומרת יום כנגד יום is forbidden only in full relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case really is about relations in the normal way. The judges said that the Torah's ban on העראה was written about a menstruating woman (a נדה), not about a שומרת יום כנגד יום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 27 by giving a new mistaken ruling that fits only a שומרת יום כנגד יום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about העראה uses the words אשה דוה, which describes a נדה. The judges read this to mean the ban on העראה covers only a נדה, so for a שומרת יום כנגד יום they permitted העראה. That is a misreading of a פסוק, not a denial of something written openly, so the בית דין can be liable. This also explains why the משנה picked a שומרת יום כנגד יום and not a נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really. It brings back an earlier idea and fixes it.
In the normal way of relations
A woman who is unwell, meaning a נדה
A woman who saw blood during the days of זיבה and must wait one clean day

phrases.english: Rather, actually, it is about relations in the normal way,
and it is where the judges said:
The ban on initial contact is about an afflicted woman,
phrases.notes: The פסוק about העראה (ויקרא 20:18) says אשה דוה, so the judges claimed it only covers a regular נדה.

phrases.english: that is what is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 27 by finding a ruling that applies only to a שומרת יום כנגד יום and not to a נדה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mistake was about העראה שלא כדרכה, which would apply to a נדה too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mistake was limiting the העראה ban to a נדה, so it permits העראה כדרכה only for a שומרת יום כנגד יום.

steps.title: Another answer: the judges said a זבה can only come from daytime bleeding
steps.stepSummary: Another option: the judges ruled that bleeding at night does not count toward זיבה, based on the words 'all the days of her discharge'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you like, say that the judges ruled: a woman only becomes a זבה from bleeding during the day, because the פסוק says 'all the days of her discharge'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to explain the משנה's case of a שומרת יום כנגד יום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The judges read the word 'days' in the פסוק as excluding nights. So a woman who saw blood at night would not be a שומרת יום at all, and they would permit her completely. This also comes from reading a פסוק, so it is not something the צדוקים openly agree to, and the בית דין can be liable.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say. It brings a second answer.
A woman with a discharge of blood outside her regular period

phrases.english: And if you wish, say that they said:
A woman is only a זבה from bleeding in the daytime,
as it is written: 'All the days of her discharge.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:26

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the same question from step 27.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only possible mistake was about which kinds of relations are forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mistake could also be about who counts as a זבה at all: the judges said nighttime bleeding does not count.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's case of שומרת יום כנגד יום works either because the judges limited the העראה ban to a נדה, or because they said nighttime bleeding does not make a זבה.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה's case of carrying on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a בית דין is liable for ruling that carrying from one domain to another on שבת is permitted. But carrying out is written openly in a פסוק, so why are they liable?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: if they said there is שבת in the Torah, but one who carries from one domain to another is exempt, they are liable. But why? Carrying out is written openly: 'Do not carry a burden out of your houses'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new example from the משנה that seems to go against the rule of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to that rule, a בית דין is not liable for permitting something openly written in the Torah. Carrying out on שבת is openly written in ירמיהו, so ruling it permitted should be plain ignorance. Yet the משנה says the בית דין is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying out from a private area to a public area
Domain, an area such as private or public

phrases.english: We learned: There is שבת in the Torah,
but one who carries from one domain to another is exempt.
And why should the בית דין be liable?
Carrying out is written openly:
'Do not carry a burden out of your houses'!
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 17:22

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The case of שומרת יום כנגד יום is settled, so the גמרא moves to the next example in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל that a בית דין is not liable for permitting something openly written in the Torah
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes the בית דין liable for permitting carrying, but carrying out is written openly in a פסוק.

steps.title: The judges said only carrying out is forbidden, carrying in is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The case is where the judges said the פסוק forbids only carrying out, and permitted carrying in.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is where they said: carrying out is forbidden, but carrying in is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the judges did not deny the פסוק. They only permitted carrying in, which the פסוק does not mention openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks only of carrying out of your houses. Carrying in from public to private is not written openly, so the צדוקים would not agree it is forbidden. A mistaken ruling about it can make the בית דין liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying in from a public area to a private area

phrases.english: It is where they said: Carrying out is what is forbidden,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording; the usual printed גמרא doesn't have them.

phrases.english: but carrying in is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 30.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The judges permitted all carrying, even carrying out.
steps.terutzMaskana: The judges permitted only carrying in, which is not written openly.

steps.title: Another answer: the judges permitted handing over and throwing
steps.stepSummary: Another option: the judges agreed carrying out and carrying in are forbidden, but permitted handing or throwing an object from one domain to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you like, say that they said: carrying out and carrying in are forbidden, but handing across and throwing are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to explain the משנה's case of carrying on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the judges accept both carrying out and carrying in. Their mistake is about moving an object without walking with it, by handing it or throwing it. Since this is not written openly in the Torah, the בית דין can be liable for permitting it.

keyTerms.meaning: One who hands an object across from one domain to another
One who throws an object from one domain to another

phrases.english: And if you wish, say
that they said: Carrying out and carrying in are what is forbidden,
but handing across and throwing are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, דְּאָמְרִי: הוֹצָאָה וְהַכְנָסָה הוּא דַּאֲסִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the question from step 30.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mistake had to be about carrying in.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mistake could also be about handing or throwing, while agreeing that both carrying out and carrying in are forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: The שבת case in the משנה works either because the judges permitted carrying in, or because they permitted handing and throwing. Neither is written openly in the Torah.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה's case of bowing to an idol
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a בית דין is liable for ruling that one who bows to an idol is exempt. But bowing is written openly in the Torah, so why are they liable?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: if they said there is עבודה זרה in the Torah, but one who bows is exempt, they are liable. But why? Bowing is written openly: 'Do not bow to another god'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the next example from the משנה against the rule of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל. This sets up the answer that will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah openly forbids bowing to another god. Permitting it should be plain ignorance, which the צדוקים would also recognize. So why does the משנה make the בית דין liable?

phrases.english: We learned: There is idol worship in the Torah,
but one who bows is exempt.
And why should the בית דין be liable?
Bowing is written openly,
as it is written: 'Do not bow to another god'!
phrases.notes: שמות 34:14

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the שבת case is answered, the גמרא brings the next example in the משנה with the same kind of challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל that a בית דין is not liable for permitting something openly written in the Torah
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes the בית דין liable for permitting bowing, but bowing to another god is written openly in a פסוק.

steps.title: The judges permitted bowing that is not the idol's normal way of worship
steps.stepSummary: The case is where the judges said bowing is forbidden only when it is that idol's normal type of worship, and permitted it otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where they said: bowing is forbidden only when that is the idol's normal way of being worshipped. But when it is not its normal way, bowing is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 33. The judges did not permit all bowing. They limited the איסור to idols that are normally served by bowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that bowing is written openly in the Torah, so under שמואל's rule permitting it should not count as a ruling. The answer is that the judges agreed bowing can be forbidden and only limited it to an idol whose normal service is bowing. The פסוק does not openly say whether bowing is forbidden to an idol not usually served that way, so the צדוקים would not agree, and the בית דין can be liable.

keyTerms.meaning: In its normal way (the usual way this idol is worshipped)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the judges permitted bowing to idols in general. They kept the איסור for idols worshipped by bowing and permitted only the other cases. The point is that the part they permitted is not openly written in the פסוק.

phrases.english: Where they said: when bowing is forbidden, it is in its normal way,
phrases.notes: "They" means the judges of the בית דין. "Its normal way" means the way that particular idol is usually worshipped.

phrases.english: but when it is not its normal way, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 33 by defining a case of a partial ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation: the judges permitted only part of the איסור, not all of it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed the judges permitted bowing that a clear פסוק forbids, so the צדוקים would agree and the judges should be exempt under שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: They forbade bowing only when it is the idol's normal worship and permitted it otherwise. The פסוק does not openly forbid that second case, so they are liable.

steps.title: The judges permitted a bow without stretching out the arms and legs
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: the judges said only a full bow with arms and legs stretched out is forbidden, and permitted a smaller bow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you could say: the case is where they said that bowing itself is forbidden only in its normal form, which includes stretching out the arms and legs. A bow without stretching out the arms and legs is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the question from Step 33. This time the judges narrowed what counts as "bowing" in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 34 the limit was about the idol, meaning whether bowing is its normal service. Here the limit is about the act itself: only a full bow with arms and legs stretched out counts. The פסוק does not openly say that a smaller bow is forbidden, so permitting it is not something the צדוקים would agree is wrong, and the judges can be liable.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say instead (introduces another answer)
Stretching out the arms and legs (lying fully flat)

steps.whatToRemember: All three cases in the משנה (נדה, שבת, עבודה זרה) are explained the same way. The judges accepted the פסוק but permitted a detail that the פסוק does not openly state, so שמואל's rule still holds. In Step 34 the limit was about which idol. In Step 35 the limit was about what kind of bow.

phrases.english: And if you want, say: where they said:
bowing itself is forbidden only in its normal way,
which has stretching out of the arms and legs in it,

phrases.aramaic: הָא הִשְׁתַּחֲוָיָה דְּלֵית בַּהּ פִּשּׁוּט יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם – שַׁרְיָא.
phrases.english: but bowing that does not have stretching out of the arms and legs in it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, דְּאָמְרִי: הִשְׁתַּחֲוָיָה גּוּפַהּ כְּדַרְכָּהּ הוּא דַּאֲסִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, alternative answer to the קשיא of Step 33, alongside Step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the definition of the act: only full bowing with arms and legs stretched out is forbidden.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed the judges permitted bowing that an open פסוק forbids, so they should be exempt under שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: They forbade full bowing and permitted a smaller bow. The פסוק does not openly forbid the smaller bow, so they are liable.
